To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the direct angle mapping method can be used to map the human motion to the robot motion, (2) the ANFIS method can be used as a fast solution to the inverse kinematics of a humanoid robot, and (3) the iterative Jacobian method can also be used to solve the inverse kinematic problem.
the inverse kinematic model of a humanoid robot can be found using human arm lengths, and that the inverse kinematics can be solved iteratively using the pseudo-inverse Jacobian matrix.

(i) the direct mapping approach is the simplest and fastest but the accuracy is low; (ii) the inverse kinematics using adaptive neural network is the most accurate but the slowest and (iii) the iterative approach is the most accurate and fastest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to use the human upper body motion to drive the upper body of a humanoid robot in real-time.
developing an efficient and accurate inverse kinematic model for the humanoid robot to imitate human arm motion.
the development of a humanoid robot capable of imitating human upper body motion using a Kinect sensor as the human interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ANFIS based inverse kinematics model is more accurate than the Jacobian based model.
the ANFIS based approach is the most suitable method to solve the inverse kinematic problem for a humanoid robot.
all the three methods are able to imitate the human motion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fuzzy logic based inverse kinematics method outperformed the other two methods.
the fuzzy logic approach is more accurate and faster than the Jacobian approach.
the fuzzy logic approach is faster but not accurate and the Jacobian method is accurate and fast.

the inverse kinematics of a humanoid robot can be solved using a Kinect sensor.
the fuzzy logic based inverse kinematics model performs better than the other two methods.
